D.exposure: All source rows and 2026 vote-type concentration are known before this prereg; explicitly post-hoc, not blinded design

A: Is the unadjusted difference in cross-party group-majority agreement 2025→2026 a period effect after exact standardization on suspension-of-rules voting procedure?
estimand: Descriptive standardized risk difference in shared party yea-majority: 2026 minus 2025 among fixed 6+6 roll calls; stratify two types suspension vs other

B.H1: Year difference entirely explained arithmetically by procedure mix in this fixed 12-roll sample; within each stratum both years same agreement rate
B.H0: Year difference persists conditional on procedure
B.Halt: Case mix and very small dates; within-year vote issues nonexchangeable, not causal mediation identification

C: Compute raw 2025 and 2026 shared-majority proportions; two-by-two counts for suspension and other per year; direct-standardize each year to pooled 50/50 as well as 2025 and 2026 procedure weights; compare expected year difference; if no common support or stratum zero count mark invalid (both strata present here, observed before prereg), no p-value or individual association; report dates and number of independent calendar sessions.
F: Procedural class is not randomized; direct standardization is a descriptive reweighting of recorded division-level outcomes, not evidence of a causal effect
G: No independent US external source or prospective holdout; both years from one House
J: If attenuation complete, record an empirical local Simpson-style composition check (not claim of new sociology); proceed to source-backed reproducibility and date clustering robustness.
